steps_tex: (i): $3 \times T$ ends in $T$, so $T$ is $0$ or $5$; $T = 5$ fails because $3 \times U + 1$ cannot end in $U$, and $T = 0$ gives $50 \times 3 = 150$.
(ii): $AB \times 5$ has two digits, so $AB$ is at most $19$, and $A$ is $1$; $19 \times 5 = 95$.
(iii): $2 \times N$ ends in $P$ and $2 \times 2$ plus the carry gives $N$, so $N$ is $4$ or $5$: $124 \times 2 = 248$ and $125 \times 2 = 250$.
(iv): $XY \times 4$ has two digits, so $X$ is $1$ or $2$, and $4 \times Y$ ends in $X$, so $X$ is $2$; $23 \times 4 = 92$.
(v): $PP \times QQ$ is $P \times Q \times 121$, and a $3$-digit product needs $P \times Q$ to be at most $8$.
The units digit of the product is then $P \times Q$ itself, and it must be $P$, so $Q = 1$: $22 \times 11 = 242$, $33 \times 11 = 363$, $44 \times 11 = 484$.
(vi): $KKK$ divided by $6$ must be a $2$-digit number ending in $K$: $222$, $444$, $666$ and $888$ give $37$, $74$, $111$ and $148$, and only $74$ ends in $4$; $74 \times 6 = 444$.

item.question: Your partner has two pawns in a line with the third point empty, and it is your turn to place a pawn. What should you do, and why?
steps: If you leave the empty point, your partner completes a line of three next turn.
A completed line lets your partner remove one of your pawns.
Placing your pawn on the empty point blocks the line.
item.answer: Place your pawn on the empty point to block the line of three
